holidays.name: International Axe Throwing Day
holidays.description: Grab your safety goggles and your competitive spirit. This day celebrates the thunk of a well-aimed axe hitting a bullseye. It's a day for lumberjack-style fun, with friends cheering and trash-talking in equal measure.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its origin is unclear. It has grown alongside the popularity of recreational axe-throwing leagues and venues.
holidays.funFact: Modern axe-throwing bars have spread across the world, and organized leagues now hold competitions with standardized targets and rules.

holidays.name: National Sewing Machine Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble machine that stitches up everything from wedding gowns to superhero capes. Dust off your bobbin, thread the needle, and mend that pile of clothes you've been ignoring.
holidays.origin: The day honors the invention of the sewing machine and is tied to Elias Howe, who is credited with a patent for a lockstitch machine. It is an unofficial observance.
holidays.funFact: Elias Howe reportedly got the idea of putting the thread hole at the needle's point from a dream, though the story is often retold as legend.

holidays.name: National Kitchen Klutzes of America Day
holidays.description: A day for everyone who has dropped an egg, burned toast, or set off the smoke alarm while cooking. Laugh at your kitchen mishaps and be gentle with yourself, because even great cooks have spills.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrated by home cooks who embrace their clumsy side.
holidays.funFact: Kitchen accidents are among the most common household mishaps, which makes this day relatable for almost everyone who cooks.
